title: Conservative SLO Lattice for Safe Batching & Cache Tuning
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Automated batch/cache tuning can reduce cost but may increase tail latency or regress throughput in subtle ways. Existing tuning flows can apply aggressive profiles too quickly or without conservative fallbacks, causing customer-facing latency spikes or throughput degradation.

Proposal: Implement a conservative SLO 'lattice' that governs automated batching and cache profile recommendations and their application. The lattice is a layered set of guardrails: pre-apply validation (shadow traffic + offline sim), staged apply (canary traffic fractions + SLO-aware routing), runtime limiters (rate & concurrency caps tied to SLO headroom), and automatic anomaly-based rollback. Add a confidence scoring mechanism for recommendations so less-certain suggestions can only be applied under stricter limits. Integrate with existing observability (per-route p50/p95/p99, error budget, cost deltas) and routing components to enable safe fallback to baseline model/profile variants when anomalies are detected.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine emits a confidence score for each batching/cache profile suggestion and stores it in the recommendations table.
Shadow-apply pipeline runs sampled traffic through the candidate profile without impacting production and reports p50/p95/p99 deltas and throughput impact within 24h.
Canary apply mechanism supports staged traffic fractions (1%, 5%, 25%) and enforces runtime limiters that cap concurrency and request rate for canary hosts.

SLO-lattice automatic rollback triggers when either: (a) p99 latency increases beyond configurable delta and error budget consumption > threshold, or (b) throughput drops > configured percentage compared to baseline for 10 minutes.
Dashboard panels and alerts for SLO-lattice decisions (shadow results, canary metrics, anomalies, rollbacks) are available in Console under Optimize -> Recommendations.
End-to-end tests simulate regression scenarios and verify automatic rollback triggers within defined windows without manual intervention.
Runbook and operator controls (pause/resume, force-apply, revert) documented and accessible in the console.
No customer-facing SLOs are violated for >5 minutes during staged rollouts in canary experiments in 95% of test runs.
plan: Design: finalize SLO-lattice policies and confidence buckets (high/medium/low) with Product and Observability - 1 week
Infra: extend the recommendations service schema to include confidence, shadow-run flags, and applied_profile metadata - 3d
Shadowing: implement sampled shadow-run pipeline that mirrors requests to a candidate serving path and aggregates metric deltas - 2 weeks
Canary: add staged apply plumbing to router to assign traffic fractions and attach limiter tokens tied to SLO headroom - 2 weeks
Limiters: implement dynamic concurrency and rate caps that reference per-route SLO budgets and enforce conservative defaults - 1 week
Anomaly detection: build EWMA + outlier detector on p50/p95/p99 and throughput with configurable windows and hysteresis - 1 week
Rollback orchestration: implement auto-revert hooks and safety state machine with operator overrides - 1 week
Dashboard & Alerts: wire metrics and decision logs to Console and create on-call alerts - 4d
Testing & Runbook: end-to-end tests, chaos scenarios, and operator documentation - 1 week
implementation_notes: Use existing recommendation store but add a 'confidence' enum and 'shadow_run_id' string for traceability.
Shadow runs must be rate-limited to a small percent (default 0.5%) and tagged for sample bias analysis.
Canary routing should prefer hosts in the same region as origin traffic to avoid cross-region artifacts in latency signals.
Limiters compute headroom by comparing current burn rate to allocated error budget; caps should be proportional to remaining headroom with a minimum floor.
Anomaly detector uses parallel metrics: latency deltas, throughput ratio, and internal infra errors (OOM, GPU queue drops). A decision requires at least two signals to avoid noisy rollbacks.
Confidence scoring combines historical savings for similar workloads, model/token length distribution match, and recent stability of the route (low-variance baseline preferred).
All decisions and metric snapshots must be logged to DecisionLog (for audits and postmortems).
testing_plan: Unit tests for confidence scoring logic and limiter math.
Integration tests for shadow-run pipeline verifying no production side effects and accurate delta reporting.
Controlled canary experiments in staging with injected latency regressions and throughput reductions to assert rollback behavior.
Load tests to ensure limiters gracefully cap traffic without introducing queueing cascades.
Chaos test: randomly kill canary hosts and ensure fallback to baseline works and no unavailable routes are exposed to customers.
Long-running drift test: run several low-impact shadow runs for 48h and verify stability of metrics aggregation and noise filtering.
rollout_strategy: Phase 0 (internal): deploy shadowing and decision logging to internal account only. Collect 72h of baseline comparisons.
Phase 1 (canary): enable staged canary for low-volume non-critical routes with conservative confidence threshold (high only) and strict limiters (1% traffic max).
Phase 2 (broader): widen candidate set to medium-confidence recommendations and raise traffic caps after 1 week of stable metrics.
Phase 3 (opt-in): expose recommendation apply UI in Console for opt-in customers with detailed impact forecasts and force-apply controls.
Phase 4 (auto): enable automated apply/rollback for high-confidence profiles with full SLO-lattice protection and operator notifications.
